title: Episode 2: Fareed Mosavat on Growth Loops
speaker: Fareed Mosavat
content:
Lenny: Fareed, you led growth at Slack, Instacart, and now Reforge. What's the biggest misconception about growth?

Fareed: That growth is about tactics - hacks, channels, viral loops. Growth is a system, not a bag of tricks. The companies that win build growth models, not growth hacks.

Lenny: What's a growth model?

Fareed: A growth model maps how your product grows. It answers: How do new users discover you? How do they activate? How do they retain? How do they refer others? It's a mathematical model of your flywheel. At Slack, our model was: Teams discover → Create workspace → Invite teammates → Teammates activate → Workspace retains → Workspace expands.

Lenny: How do you build one?

Fareed: Start with the 'North Star Metric' - the one metric that captures value delivery. For Slack it was 'daily active users in paid workspaces'. Then work backwards: what drives that? Messages sent. What drives messages? Active channels. What drives channels? Team size. Now you have your model.

Lenny: What about growth loops vs funnels?

Fareed: Funnels are linear - users enter, some convert, rest drop off. Loops are circular - output of one cycle becomes input of the next. A referral loop: User joins → Invites friends → Friends join → They invite more. The loop compounds. Funnels degrade; loops accelerate.

Lenny: Can you share a specific loop from Instacart?

Fareed: The 'shopper loop'. More shoppers → Faster delivery → Higher customer satisfaction → More orders → More shopper earnings → More shoppers. Each turn of the loop improved the experience. We invested heavily in shopper supply because it drove the entire flywheel.

Lenny: How do you measure loop health?

Fareed: Loop velocity (how fast it turns), loop volume (how many users per turn), and loop efficiency (conversion at each step). At Reforge, we teach teams to instrument every step. If you can't measure it, you can't improve it.

Lenny: What's your advice for building a growth team?

Fareed: Don't start with a 'growth team'. Start with a growth model. Then hire for the constraints in your model. If activation is the bottleneck, hire a product manager + engineer + designer focused on activation. Structure follows strategy.

Lenny: Any counter-intuitive insights?

Fareed: Retention is the new acquisition. Improving retention by 5% can increase profits by 25-95% (Bain). But everyone obsesses over top-of-funnel. The best growth teams spend 60%+ of their time on retention and expansion.
